reason: README gives a pip-installable `protenix pred` CLI that runs structure prediction from a JSON file with public weights, feasible on CPU for a small protein without MSA.
demo: README 'Quick Prediction': protenix pred -i ... -o ... -n protenix_base_default_v1.0.0 (CPU-usable flags from inference_demo.sh / docs)
goal: Install Protenix (README: pip install protenix, or from the /work/Protenix clone) on this CPU-only machine so that `protenix pred -i <input.json> -o <outdir> -n protenix_base_default_v1.0.0 --use_msa false -d fp32 -c 4 -p 20 -e 1 --trimul_kernel torch --triatt_kernel torch` works on a small single-chain protein JSON (format like examples/input.json) and writes predicted structure .cif files plus confidence json under the output directory. Model weights are downloaded automatically. Provide /work/env.sh (activating the environment) and make the command work from /work/Protenix.
check: The hidden test runs protenix pred on a 76-residue protein and verifies a predicted mmCIF with the full atom set and plausible backbone geometry, and a confidence summary json with a reasonable pLDDT.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Oracle runs `protenix pred` without the documented kernel options; the CLI defaults are --trimul_kernel/--triatt_kernel 'cuequivariance' (CUDA-only), so a CPU user following the docs (who would pass --trimul_kernel torch --triatt_kernel torch) cannot make the oracle's exact command work without patching the repo; the passing run patched runner/inference.py to change the defaults. v2 passes the documented torch kernels.

Oracle is lenient: pipeline exit status ignored (no pipefail) and only file size / ATOM count are checked; a broken model that writes an atom cloud passes. v2 checks 76 CA atoms, CA-CA backbone spacing ~3.8 A, and summary pLDDT > 50 (the run reported ~76 with the same settings).
Goal phrase 'avoid anything needing GPU-only kernels' is a workaround hint; replaced by the documented flags in the command itself.
evidence: src/bytedance-protenix/inference_demo.sh header - documents -c/-p/-e/-d/--use_msa and kernel options incl. 'torch'
src/bytedance-protenix/docs/training_inference_instructions.md:101,109-111,131 - --use_msa false, dtype, kernel flags; CUDA kernels enabled by default
data/runs/bytedance-protenix/deliverables/NOTES.md item 4 - 'CLI defaults to cuequivariance ... crashes ... (and still exits 0)'; patched runner/inference.py
src/bytedance-protenix/runner/dumper.py:199,267 and protenix/model/sample_confidence.py:112 - output names and plddt on 0-100 scale
